quote: Within the oasis, c. 4 km. long and 0.6 km. wide
notes: 'c.' values, km converted to m; more than twenty springs; Hebrew ʿEnot Suqim. Map ref. printed '1249/1929' for the oasis/excavation without naming the grid (grid_system unknown); repeated as site_grid on rows in Areas A and B.

quote: Area A to the north of the spring
notes: The ʿEin Feshkha spring: Area A lies north of it, Area B in the cliff west of it. No size or other attribute; row kept as a relation target. The industrial channels were fed by now dried-up springs north of the site (no rows).

quote: The cliff, c. 100 m. high, descends almost vertically to the shore
notes: Bounds the southern end of the oasis (Hebrew Rosh Suqim); height 'c.'; elevation at its foot -393 m; leaves only a narrow passage along the shore.

quote: A steep path named Macaleh Feshkha climbs to the south-west
notes: Climbs SW from ʿEin Feshkha toward the Valley of Hyrcania; p. 66: runs to the west of the Area B tower. Direction is the path's course, not an opening, so opening_dirs blank. 'Macaleh' is the extraction's OCR of Maʿaleh.

period: Early Roman (reign of Herod to c. 130 CE)
quote: located c. 100 m. north of Feshkha and only a few metres
notes: Site c. 4,000 sq.m. with three elements (main building, industrial complex, square enclosure); c. 100 m N of Feshkha (spring), a few metres from the steep slope bordering the oasis on the west.

quote: external dimensions: 18 24 m.; 432 sq.m. in area, including courtyard
notes: Printed '18 24 m.' (multiplication sign lost in the extraction); length/width keyed in printed order. height_m = preserved wall height, printed '2 m. or more'. Exterior walls 1 m thick, fieldstones bound with mortar; doorways of Samra sandstone ashlars. n_openings/opening_dirs = the two entrances in the east-facing facade W3 (the only external openings described). Staircase implies an upper storey. Three late-1st-c. CE tombs along the outer face of its southern wall (hir04:tombs_S_wall).

quote: In the structure's façade (W3), which faces east, there is a main entrance
notes: width_m = thickness from the general statement that exterior walls are 1 m thick (p. 44). Contains hir04:W3.door_main and hir04:W3.door_N.

quote: a main entrance (0.7 m. wide), leading directly into the courtyard
notes: In facade W3, which faces east; doorways built of ashlars (general statement, p. 44).

quote: an additional entrance (0.6 m. wide), leading into the rooms of the northern wing
notes: In facade W3 (faces east); which northern-wing rooms it enters is not stated; not stated whether it is the common entrance of hir04:Nwing_E_rooms (fig. 15).

quote: The courtyard is fairly spacious (7.8x11.8 m.; 92 sq.m. in area)
notes: 92 sq.m., 21% of the building; floor of tamped clay at -386.00 m; square pillar 1x1 m at its western end (western end probably roofed); later additions L117 (NW corner) and L154 (separated by W13).

quote: At its western end a square pillar (lxl m.) is preserved
notes: 'lxl' is the extraction's OCR of 1x1. Apparently supported the terrace of the upper storey. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: In the north-western corner (Locus 117) there was a small cell (2.2x2.8 m.)
notes: In the NW corner of the courtyard; divided in two by partition wall W19; walls W17 and W18 roughly built, a later addition; = de Vaux's Locus 6 (storage jar buried to its shoulders in the floor); opus sectile tiles on its floor; possibly a pantry.

quote: Locus 154, a long, narrow room (1.8x8 m.)
notes: Separated from the courtyard by wall W13 (perpendicular to the facade, carelessly built, later addition); stone mortar in its corner at the NE corner of the courtyard.

quote: The interior space of the mortar is conical, with a depth of 0.3 m.
notes: In the NE corner of the courtyard, in the corner of L154; conical interior; probably for food processing.

quote: In the southern wing of the structure a staircase was preserved
notes: Contains hir04:staircase_S flanked by hir04:L118 (E) and hir04:L106-114 (W). Parent row; feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: a flight of six stairs (fig. 7) is preserved in the southern wing
notes: Staircase 0.9 m wide, bordered on each side by a room; indicates an upper storey (reconstruction fig. 8). feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: The eastern room, Locus 118, is spacious (4.3x5.6 m.)
notes: East of the southern-wing staircase.

quote: the long, narrow western room (3x8.8 m.) is divided into two loci (106 and 114)
notes: West of the staircase; divided into L106 and L114 by narrow partition wall W16; local id joins the two locus numbers (keyer's).

quote: divided into two loci (106 and 114) by a narrow partition wall (W16)
notes: Part of the western room of the southern wing; which part (N or S) not stated; W16 separates it from L114.

quote: divided into two loci (106 and 114) by a narrow partition wall (W16)
notes: Part of the western room of the southern wing; which part (N or S) not stated; W16 separates it from L106.

quote: The façade wall (W5), preserved to a height of 2.2 m., contains a single doorway
notes: Wing west of the courtyard, higher building standard: large stones 0.8 m long, thickened foundations, walls thicker than the other wings (to carry the upper storey); two fairly large rooms (hir04:W_wing_S_room, hir04:L104). n_openings = the single doorway in facade W5; its facing direction is not stated.

quote: The façade wall (W5), preserved to a height of 2.2 m.
notes: height_m = preserved height. Contains one doorway (hir04:W5.door).

quote: The doorway (0.9 m. wide) is built of ashlars with marginal dressing.
notes: In W5; opens into the southernmost room of the western wing; a stone step in front of the threshold (n_steps 1, outside); triangular lamp niche in its southern jamb (hir04:W5.door.niche). Facing direction not stated.

quote: This small niche (base width: 18 cm.; height: 18 cm.; depth: 10 cm.)
notes: Hewn in the southern door jamb on the inner face of W5, 0.9 m above the floor; base width keyed as width_m; probably for a lamp. construction blank: cut into a built ashlar jamb, not bedrock.

quote: contains a single doorway which opens into the southernmost of the two rooms
notes: No locus number in the text (feature_id is the keyer's). Entered by hir04:W5.door; W6 (with doorway) separates it from L104.

quote: was preserved to a height of 1.5 m. A doorway (0.8 m. wide)
notes: Divides the two rooms of the western wing; height_m = preserved height; contains hir04:W6.door.

quote: A doorway (0.8 m. wide) provided access to the northern room (Locus 104)
notes: In W6. construction from the general statement that the doorways are built of ashlars (p. 44).

quote: the largest architectural space in the building (internal dimensions: 3.8 8.4 m.; 32 sq.m.
notes: Internal dims, printed '3.8 8.4 m.' (multiplication sign lost); 32 sq.m.; basalt lower grinding stone (0.36x0.65 m, 0.1 m thick) near its NW corner = de Vaux's Locus 3; awl on the floor; possibly a kitchen.

quote: The northern wing consists of three rooms whose doorways face south, towards the courtyard.
notes: Three rooms: the westernmost (hir04:Nwing_W_room, stable) and two with a common entrance (hir04:Nwing_E_rooms). n_openings blank: no total stated. Its southern wall W7 has the window (iron arrowhead embedded in W7). Facade entrance hir04:W3.door_N leads into its rooms.

quote: The westernmost room, which is fairly large (internal dimensions: 3.8x8 m.)
notes: Internal dims. n_openings = doorway onto the courtyard (blocked in a later phase) + large window in S wall W7 (hir04:W7.window), both facing S. Divided by thin partition W10 into L105 (larger western space) and an unlabelled eastern part for animals. No locus number for the whole room (feature_id is the keyer's).

quote: In the larger western space (Locus 105), signs of a fierce fire were found.
notes: West of partition W10 in the stable room; wall stones at its west end cracked and reddened by fire; possibly a straw pile in the corner. Only attribute: part of the stable room.

quote: the large window (0.8 m. wide; at least 0.8 m. high)
notes: In southern wall W7 of the animal (eastern) part of the stable, opening directly onto the courtyard; height printed 'at least 0.8 m.'; sill 0.7 m above the raised courtyard level; tethering holes in the jambs; probably held a manger. Class other (window).

quote: In the courtyard in front of the window there is a kind of ramp
notes: Facilitated access to the window/manger. feature_id is the keyer's.

class_as_printed: two rooms with a common entrance
quote: To the east of the stable are two rooms with a common entrance (fig. 15)
notes: Two rooms keyed as one row (no locus numbers or sizes given); n_openings = the common entrance; S from the statement that the northern wing's doorways face south.

quote: was found below the threshold of this entrance
notes: Fig. 15 'Northern wing entrance'; hoard of eight coins of Mattathias Antigonus (40-37 BCE) under its threshold (p. 42 'under the threshold of one of the doorways'). Direction from the statement that northern-wing doorways face south.

quote: three tombs, one next to the other, along the outer face of the southern wall
notes: Found by de Vaux in 1958 along the outer face of the main building's southern wall; three tombs keyed as one row (no numbers, sizes or orientations given here); author suggests pagan use in the site's final days.

quote: The industrial complex (fig. 18) is located to the north-east of the main building.
notes: NE of the main building; enclosed by fence walls W20, W21 (W22), c. 2,000 sq.m.; four channels, a reservoir and an installation. Trial probe L143 east of the main building (2x4 m) is an excavation unit and is not keyed.

quote: The western fence wall (W20), which runs north-south and is 12 m. long
notes: Runs N-S from the NW corner of the main building. width_m and height_m (preserved, 'about 1 m.') from the statement covering both fence walls; original height reconstructed c. 2 m.

quote: is 17 m. long and runs east-west in general direction
notes: Northern fence wall, perpendicular to W20; crossed by channels L135 and hir04:channel_2; width and preserved height ('about 1 m.') from the statement covering both fence walls.

quote: this segment is designated W22 and is preserved for a length of only 3 m.
notes: The eastern end of W21 turning south; length = preserved length; author suggests it continued south and west to the wall perpendicular to the square enclosure.

quote: one of these channels (Locus 135) is approximately 10 m. long
notes: One of two channels from now dried-up springs that cross northern fence wall W21; drains into pool L133. Fieldstone build and whitish hydraulic plaster stated for the four-channel system. Length 'approximately'.

quote: and the other is 1.5 m. long
notes: The second of the two channels from now dried-up springs crossing W21; no locus number (feature_id is the keyer's).

quote: Locus 133, a small, well-preserved square pool (1.7x1.7 m.; c. 1 m. deep)
notes: Depth 'c.'. Two channels lead out: the longer to the reservoir (channel_3), the shorter to the installation (L137). Plaster and construction of the pool itself not stated.

quote: The third channel (10 m. long; 0.5 m. wide) leads to the north-western corner
notes: From L133 to the NW corner of the reservoir; integrated in the smooth stone surface; no locus number (feature_id is the keyer's).

quote: Both channels are integrated in a smooth stone surface.
notes: Paving at -386.00 m (almost the courtyard level); channel_3 and L137 run in it; two cylindrical stones found on it by de Vaux, west of the pool (L142) and north of the channel to the reservoir. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: Since no staircase was found, we propose that this pool was intended for water storage
notes: Rectangular; walls 0.8 m thick; depth printed 'at least 3 m.' (not excavated to full depth); capacity printed 'at least 80 sq.m.' (sic). n_steps 0 from 'no staircase was found' in an incompletely excavated pool. No locus number (feature_id is the keyer's).

quote: The fourth channel (Locus 137; 2.5 m. long) fed the installation
notes: The shorter channel from L133; a branch from it (hir04:L137.branch) feeds the pool in L119.

quote: The installation consists of a large pool with two adjacent cells, western and eastern
notes: Comprises large pool L142, western cell L127 (gathering vat) and eastern cell L119 (miqweh); author interprets it as for balsam perfume essence; cells probably roofed. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: Two steps in the western wall (W33) provided access to the pool's floor.
notes: Printed '4.4 4.5 m.' (multiplication sign lost); almost square; walls c. 1 m thick; patches of whitish hydraulic plaster on floor and walls; cylindrical stone (1.48 m long, 0.6 m diam.) on the floor near the steps; drainage opening in the base of S wall W29; doorway from L127 in W29; author: soaking pool open to the sun. n_openings blank (no count stated).

quote: The opening was formed by stone drums with a round hole (10 cm. in diameter)
notes: In the base of the pool's southern wall W29 (direction keyed from the wall named); could be blocked; controlled the water level.

quote: The water was drained through a tunnel that ran under the partition wall (W29)
notes: Runs under W29 into the gathering vat in L127. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: a channel (1.1 m. long; 10x20 cm. in section), leading directly from the large pool
notes: Section printed '10x20 cm.'; first figure keyed as width, second as depth (keyer's assignment). A flat, slightly protruding stone at its end kept liquid from spilling over the vat walls. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: (W31) three steps, 0.8 m. wide, lead down to the cell's floor
notes: 8 sq.m.; plastered floor on a foundation of flat tamped fieldstones. Openings: the stepped entrance in S wall W31 (steps 0.8 m wide) and a 0.6 m doorway in N wall W29 to pool L142 (hir04:L127.door); directions keyed from the walls named. Gathering vat in the floor by E wall W36.

quote: An additional doorway, 0.6 m. wide, in the cell's northern wall (W29)
notes: Direct access from the cell to the pool to its north.

quote: The vat is square (0.9x1 m.; 1.4 m. deep; capacity: 1.26 cu.m.; fig. 23)
notes: In the floor of L127 close to E wall W36, which is the vat's E wall (hence built); a small slightly protruding stone in W36 aids descent (not called a step; n_steps blank); column drum (0.3 m diam., 0.35 m high) in situ on the floor; no connection with the pool on the other side of W36.

quote: accessed by four steps, 0.6 m. wide, leading down from the north-western corner
notes: Internal dims, 10.3 sq.m.; floor a little lower than L127's; steps 0.6 m wide; one entrance stated, at the NW corner (keyed NW); the L137 branch channel runs through its steps; fig. 25 caption calls it the 'southern cell'; author: roofed for bathers' privacy.

quote: Although only the topmost step is preserved, we assume that there were two additional ones.
notes: Printed '1.5 1.8 m.' (multiplication sign lost); capacity 2.4 cu.m.; by W36, no connection with the vat; narrow staircase 0.4 m wide inside; 1 step preserved (keyed), 3 reconstructed by the author; 'built within an enclosed cell'; author's function label miqweh.

quote: fed by a channel that branches off from the short channel mentioned above (Locus 137)
notes: Runs around the N and E walls of the large pool and through the steps of the eastern cell. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: The entrance was apparently in the eastern wall facing the main building.
notes: 1,156 sq.m.; walls 0.7 m thick; very little remains (eroded soil, Route 90 built over it); entrance 'apparently' in the E wall; row of 'about ten' pillars on the N side (n_pillars 10); stable and small room along the N side. Described from de Vaux's excavation.

quote: a row of about ten pillars, spaced approximately 2 m. apart
notes: On the northern side of the enclosure; 'about ten'; spacing c. 2 m. Same pillars as counted on hir04:enclosure. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: long narrow space between the pillars and the outer wall of the enclosure (3.5x27 m.)
notes: Between the pillar row and the enclosure's outer wall; probably a stable. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: The entrance to the room is on the east.
notes: At the eastern end of the stable; internal 3x3.5 m; for accommodation or storage. feature_id is the keyer's.

quote: exposed for a length of 12 m., starts at the south-eastern corner
notes: Runs NE from the enclosure's SE corner toward 'the wall on the east of the industrial complex' (linked to W22 by the keyer); author: the two probably joined, bounding the yard east of the main building. length = exposed length. feature_id is the keyer's.

site_name: area between ʿEin Feshkha and Qumran
quote: join to form a stretch of c. 500 m., roughly north-south in direction
notes: Fence wall between ʿEin Feshkha and Qumran from de Vaux's segments: southern 200 m segment from the enclosure's NW corner (hir04:long_wall.S) and northern 110 m segment south of Qumran (hir04:long_wall.N); the author dates it Early Roman because two segments start at Early Roman complexes; estate boundary.

quote: at the north-western corner of the square enclosure and runs north for approximately 200 m.
notes: Starts at the square enclosure's NW corner and runs N toward Qumran; = the southern segment of the long wall (p. 69 '200 m long segment').

site_name: area between ʿEin Feshkha and Qumran
quote: the 110 m long segment that runs south from the complex of Qumran
notes: Northern end of the long wall, running south from Qumran.

quote: The structure is square in plan (4.7x4.7 m.; fig. 28). Its walls, 0.8 m. thick
notes: Area B, in the cliff west of the spring, elevation -336 m; rel_distance 50 = 'c. 50 m. above' the Early Roman site (vertical). Walls 0.8 m thick, roughly squared limestone blocks (0.7x1 m avg.); E wall eroded, N and S walls only foundations, W wall one course plus one stone; fill 0.5-1 m over an ash layer; Maʿaleh Feshkha path to its west. feature_id is the keyer's.

site_name: area between ʿEin Feshkha and Qumran
quote: This was a square enclosure (c. 17 17 m.; 290 sq.m.)
notes: De Vaux's batiment israelite; c. 200 m S of Nahal Qumran and c. 80 m W of the road; c. 20 m of its NW corner preserved; wall 0.7 m wide, two courses to 0.6 m (height_m = preserved height); large fieldstones (0.4x0.5 m avg.) without mortar; original height estimated c. 2 m, upper part possibly mudbrick. Printed 'c. 17 17 m.' (multiplication sign lost). No date given by the author.

site_name: area between ʿEin Feshkha and Qumran
quote: it was a square structure (12x12 m.) with an entrance on the east (fig. 31).
notes: Close to the modern road, c. 25 m NW of ʿEnot Qumran; plan per de Vaux; walls 1.1 m thick; interior divided in two by a partition; 'pillar-like constructions' in the NE and SE corners (n_pillars 2); author suggests a columbarium (fig. 31 caption 'columbarium?'); class kept as building. No date stated (used in an Early Roman estate argument).

quote: The two springs lie east of Route 90
notes: Spring in the level area south of Nahal Qumran, east of Route 90; Tannur c. 800 m to its south; isolated building c. 25 m NW of it. Row kept as a relation target.

quote: c. 800 m. to the south, Tannur
